sections.html:
Smyrna is a compact Cobb County city of 15.4 square miles, sixteen miles out from downtown Atlanta, just west of where I-285 meets I-75 at Cumberland. Smyrna had 55,663 residents in 24,600 households at the 2020 count. Redevelopment since the early 1990s swapped townhouses and condominiums in for older neighborhoods, so look at what homes on your own block sold for lately.

One difference from most Georgia cities: Smyrna mails a property tax bill of its own, on top of the county's. Cobb Parkway (U.S. 41), Atlanta Road, South Cobb Drive (State Route 280) and I-285 pass through, and both CobbLinc and MARTA buses stop here. Buyers who commute to Cumberland, the Cobb Galleria or Midtown will care about the minutes each trip takes, so give honest times.

The terrain is typical Georgia Piedmont, with hills, broad ridges and narrow valleys. Buyers will ask about grading, drainage or retaining walls on the lot, so know what was done. The Cobb County School District runs the public schools; zones change from street to street, so send buyers to the district's address lookup.

Permit applications, building or standalone, are filed on the city's online portal. Counter submittals are no longer taken. Permits are good for six months if no activity occurs. Community Development lists these building permit charges:

FeeAmount
Building or land disturbance permit$7 per $1,000 of estimated construction cost
Records fee10 percent of the building permit fee
Standalone or MEP permit$50
Technology fee$15
Minimum building permit$125
Reinspection$50, then $100, $150 and $200 for the fourth and later

Permit and water connection fees can be reduced or waived for projects approved under the city's development incentive program. If you cannot tell which line fits your repair, phone the building division before the work begins.

An open or expired permit can surface when a buyer's inspector or a title company checks the address. Permits lapse after six months of no activity, so a repair you started and left half finished is worth looking into. Closing a permit out cleanly before you list removes one reason for a buyer to ask for a lower price. The building division is the office to ask, and it can tell you which permits it holds on file for your parcel. Do this before listing, not after a contract is signed, so any surprise is yours to fix on your own schedule.

sections.h2: Can I sell a Smyrna house that had short-term renters?
sections.html:
Yes, but tidy up the license record first. A short-term rental inside city limits must hold a Short-Term Rental License and an Occupational Tax Certificate, both applied for online. The application asks for:

  • Proof of liability insurance
  • A code compliance verification form
  • A short-term rental agent form
  • Proof of ownership
  • For owner-occupied houses, a homestead exemption or an affidavit in lieu of one

Call the Business License Coordinator at 678-631-5363 and ask if a license transfers to a buyer or has to be reissued. A rental that ran unlicensed should be straightened out with the city before you list, since a buyer's attorney can search for open compliance matters.

sections.h2: How Smyrna city taxes and Cobb County taxes fit together
sections.html:
Smyrna homeowners get two bills, one from Cobb County and one from the city. Cobb assessors set the value, and Georgia taxes 40 percent of it. Assessment notices arrive in early summer with a 45-day appeal period. County bills follow in late summer and are due in the fall.

The city bills separately, in September with payment due in November. Exemptions available through the city include $10,000 for owners aged 62 or over, $22,000 for owners with a 100 percent disability and limited income, and a homestead exemption that caps the city tax at the home's initial assessed value. File city exemption paperwork by April 1 at City Hall, 2800 King Street SE.

Unpaid city taxes lead the city to record a FIFA lien with the Cobb Superior Court clerk, letting it collect before the house can be sold. The county commissioner splits nothing between seller and buyer; liability is fixed at closing, so your contract and settlement statement assign each share.

sections.h2: Owing taxes and moving a deed
sections.html:
Partial payments are accepted by Cobb's tax commissioner. Past the due date, county taxes pick up a 5 percent penalty and monthly interest. An owner with an appeal pending still owes at least the appealed amount on time to dodge the penalty.

The county office describes four common deed types: a recorded warranty deed, a quitclaim deed, a deed of assent used for inherited property, and an executor's deed. Each is recorded with the Clerk of Superior Court. For an inherited house or a transfer inside the family, an attorney should pick the form.

Georgia's transfer tax falls on the seller unless the contract moves it, charged at $1 for the first $1,000 and 10 cents for each additional $100.

Owners with a tight deadline can weigh a standard listing against an as-is investor offer or a direct cash sale. Line up what each would put in your pocket once the bills and payoffs are settled.

sections.h2: Choosing a sale route in Smyrna
sections.html:
Three roads lead out: an agent's listing, an as-is investor sale, or a straight cash sale. Listing tends to earn the most on a house in good order, at the price of showings, inspection rounds and a lender's schedule. Selling for cash trades a lower price for a fixed closing date, handy with deferred repairs, a tenant or tax arrears.

With two tax bills in play, ask every buyer's offer to be netted against both. An unpaid city bill can become a lien, and liens must be cleared before a clean deed passes. Have your closing attorney search for liens early, and get a draft settlement statement several days ahead to read the tax lines and payoff.

sections.h2: Checklist before you accept an offer
sections.html:
1. Pull the city and county tax bills and mark which are paid.
  2. If you hosted short-term guests, make sure the license and tax records are in order.
  3. Ask building staff to confirm that repairs you made were permitted.
  4. Write into the contract who pays the transfer tax and how taxes are divided at closing.
  5. Hold an as-is cash price up against what a listing would net.
  6. For an inherited house, an attorney should choose the deed form before anything is signed.

Both cash buyers and financed buyers want tax and permit records. Having them early shortens the wait from offer to closing.

Keep a simple folder for the sale. Put the deed, both tax bills, any permit receipts and the rental license papers in it. When a buyer's attorney or a title company asks a question, you can answer in a day instead of hunting through drawers, and a quick answer keeps a good offer from cooling off.

faqs.q: Does the City of Smyrna bill its own property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Its finance department mails a separate bill in September, due in November, on top of the Cobb County one.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal my Cobb County value?
faqs.a: Forty-five days, counted from the date on your assessment notice.

faqs.q: Do I need a license for a short-term rental in Smyrna?
faqs.a: Yes, plus an Occupational Tax Certificate. Applicants provide proof of liability insurance, an agent form and proof of ownership.

faqs.q: What is the cost of a building permit in Smyrna?
faqs.a: Building permits run $7 per $1,000 of estimated construction cost, with a minimum of $125. Technology, records and reinspection fees come on top.

faqs.q: Does the county prorate taxes at closing?
faqs.a: No. Cobb's tax commissioner leaves the split to you, so your sales contract and settlement statement settle who pays.
